summary: Technical sync between Redwood and HelioCloud focused on marketplace listing requirements, reference architecture for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem), and joint solution packaging. Discussed integration checklist, network/KMS flows, required artifacts for marketplace certification, CI/CD examples, and test plan. Agreed on owners and near-term delivery dates.
topics: Reference architecture for Redwood Private on HelioCloud (VPC peering, private control plane)
Security/compliance: KMS, audit logs, SSO/SAML, data residency
Joint solution packaging and go-to-market checklist
transcript: 00:00:00 Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call? uh we'll try to keep to 45 minutes but we have 54 on the calendar. 00:00:10 Daniel Wu: hey all, Daniel here from HelioCloud, Rita and Leo are with me. 00:00:15 Alex Morgan: perfect, Alex from Redwood, Priya is our solutions engineer and Mina on the integration kit. 00:00:25 Priya Desai: hey, hi. 00:00:30 Sofia Alvarez: Sofia from Helio marketplace team, i'll mostly be listening for listing requirements. 00:00:36 Alex Morgan: ok quick agenda — marketplace listing artifacts, reference arch for private deploy in HelioCloud, CI/CD examples, security checklist, and next steps. sound good? 00:00:46 Daniel Wu: yep go for it. 00:00:50 Alex Morgan: cool, so first the marketplace listing: Helio we typically need a listing checklist — logo, screenshots, short & long descriptions, pricing SKU, support contact, and a validated deployment template. we'll send our sample artifact pack. 00:01:05 Sofia Alvarez: yes we require validated deployment template or AMI/container image, and a reference arch doc. we also have a marketplace security attestation form. 00:01:15 Alex Morgan: good — Priya, do you want to talk about what the validated deployment looks like for Redwood? 00:01:20 Priya Desai: sure. for Redwood Private we provide a control-plane package and a runtime bundle. recommended pattern is Helio customers deploy a private control-plane in their VPC with peering to Redwood-managed model serving infra or run fully self-hosted with our on-prem package. key pieces are: VPC peering or private link, KMS integration for keys, and audit log shipping. 00:01:45 Rita Nguyen: can you clarify the KMS flow? we use Helio KMS for keys in our region and we need to know if Redwood will call our KMS or we ship encrypted artifacts? 00:01:55 Priya Desai: great question. two supported flows: 1) customer-managed KMS where Redwood control plane references customer key via wrapped-Key approach and we never hold plaintext keys; or 2) if the customer wants fully private on-prem, the key material remains local and the runtime uses local HSM. we'll document both. note: some partners prefer bringing their own KMS because of data residency. 00:02:20 Leo Harris: for the peering we have transit VPCs and bandwidth limits; how chatty is the control plane? what's the number of control-plane calls per minute? 00:02:28 Mina Park: control-plane traffic is light — heartbeats, configuration updates, metrics. token-level inference stays in the runtime; for hosted we can route by policy. we'll provide an empirical profile: eg control-plane ~ 1-2 rps during spikes per cluster, telemetry batched. 00:02:45 Daniel Wu: ok that seems fine. any special ports or security groups? 00:02:50 Priya Desai: we'll share a security group list; typically 443 and a few gRPC ports for internal. we'll include a minimal allowed-inbound list and TLS certificate expectations. 00:03:05 Alex Morgan: on the listing side, Helio requires a tech contact and a test account we can use to validate deployment. Sofia, is that still the policy? 00:03:12 Sofia Alvarez: yes we need a sandbox that reproduces the marketplace onboarding flow; this is standard. 00:03:18 Alex Morgan: great — we'll provide that; Mina will create a sandbox deploy script. 00:03:25 Mina Park: on the automation front, we recommend Terraform modules for infra and Helm for runtime. we have a repo with examples. we'll share a small module that sets up the VPC peering, subnets, and service endpoints and a helm chart with a sample autoscaling config. 00:03:42 Rita Nguyen: does Redwood support EKS, GKE, and bare metal? our customers use all three. 00:03:49 Priya Desai: yes — supported orchestrators include EKS/GKE/AKS and a supported bare-metal kube distro for on-prem. for bare-metal we have different kernel/optimizer choices and we'll include recommended kernel tunings in the reference arch. 00:04:05 Leo Harris: what about quantization and hardware — any constraints for GPU types? some of our customers choose different instance classes. 00:04:13 Mina Park: runtime is hardware-aware — we ship optimized kernels for common GPU families and have fallback CPU-quantized paths. we'll include a compatibility matrix that maps model variants to recommended instance families and perf expectations. 00:04:30 Daniel Wu: good to have that, we need clear matrix for marketplace listing. 00:04:35 Alex Morgan: security/compliance — we know Helio requires SOC2 and regional data residency checks. Redwood supports SOC2, has audit logs, and SSO via SAML/SCIM. Priya can you outline the audit log flow? 00:04:47 Priya Desai: sure — audit logs can be pushed to customer-managed S3 or to Helio logging endpoints via secure shipper. logs include request metadata, model/version, and token counts. PII is not stored by default and we can redact or avoid logging prompt text depending on contract. 00:05:05 Rita Nguyen: redaction is important. can we see a sample log? 00:05:09 Priya Desai: yes we'll share sample log schema and a small pipeline for shipping. 00:05:15 Alex Morgan: on SSO, customers want SAML integration and RBAC. Redwood supports SAML and granular roles; we'll share a guide. 00:05:24 Sofia Alvarez: marketplace also needs a documented support SLA and contact method. 00:05:28 Sam Ortiz: for the marketplace listing we typically propose two SKUs: hosted API listing and dedicated/private listing. pricing and SLA differ; we'll draft recommended list prices and an enterprise sales motion. 00:05:40 Daniel Wu: marketplace cert process — how long does Redwood usually take to produce artifacts? 00:05:45 Alex Morgan: early artifacts we can share within a week: listing copy, screenshots, reference arch draft, Terraform snippets. full validation with sandbox can take 2-3 weeks depending on scheduling. 00:05:58 Mina Park: for joint solution packaging we recommend a reference architecture doc, a quickstart repo, and a joint solution brief for customers. Helio should also decide if they want Helio-managed deployment or customer self-service via the marketplace tile. 00:06:15 Rita Nguyen: prefer Helio-managed for initial GTM then offer BYO for enterprise. 00:06:21 Leo Harris: about telemetry/compatibility tests — what does Redwood need from us? 00:06:25 Priya Desai: a test account with network access, API keys for a sandbox, sample workload traces (token distribution and seq lengths), and permission to run a small benchmark. ideally a representative app. 00:06:38 Daniel Wu: we can provide sample traces but need to check internal privacy. 00:06:42 Alex Morgan: totally fine — synthetic traces also work; we just need approximate seq length and concurrency patterns. 00:06:50 Sofia Alvarez: marketplace QA — do you have an automated test harness? 00:06:54 Mina Park: we have a CI test suite that runs smoke, perf, and security checks against the deployed tile; it'll be in the quickstart repo. 00:07:05 Alex Morgan: ok let's talk about rollout plan — MVP listing: 1) basic marketplace tile with deployment template and docs; 2) reference arch and joint solution brief; 3) optional managed service offering. timeframe target: publish tile in Helio marketplace by end of January if artifacts delivered on schedule. 00:07:28 Daniel Wu: Jan end is aggressive but feasible. 00:07:33 Priya Desai: technical detail — network ports again, also want to call out KV cache traffic: when using hosted runtime we sometimes stream KV caches for warm starts; for fully private it stays local. document will clarify. 00:07:48 Leo Harris: streaming KV cache sounds like something Egress policy teams will ask about — does that send any prompt data? 00:07:54 Priya Desai: no prompt text isn't sent — KV only stores model cache states (no customer input). we'll provide a data-flow diagram in the ref arch. 00:08:05 Alex Morgan: one common obstacle is pricing SKU alignment. Sofia, can you share marketplace SKU templates so we map Redwood SKUs? 00:08:12 Sofia Alvarez: yes will send the SKU spreadsheet. 00:08:16 Sam Ortiz: we'll draft two SKUs and map to Helio fields and share by Monday. 00:08:22 Alex Morgan: ok action item recap — Alex will send checklist, Priya ref-arch, Mina terraform/helm, Helio to share diagrams and test account. 00:08:33 Daniel Wu: sounds good. 00:08:35 Rita Nguyen: quick question on support: do you provide RUNBOOKS for on-call? 00:08:39 Mina Park: yes, we provide runbooks for common incidents, escalation path, and a playbook for model regressions. we'll include SLOs for latency and availability. 00:08:50 Leo Harris: any specific observability stack integrations? we use Helio's managed Prometheus and Elastic stack. 00:08:56 Priya Desai: we have Prometheus exporters and can push traces to Jaeger/OpenTelemetry; logs to Elastic via shipper. 00:09:06 Alex Morgan: OK any blockers? 00:09:09 Daniel Wu: none immediate. need to confirm legal/security review timeline. 00:09:13 Alex Morgan: legal usually needs the marketplace agreement + security questionnaire; we can start parallel. 00:09:18 Sofia Alvarez: we'll send the vendor security questionnaire; legal will review once vendor completes. 00:09:24 Alex Morgan: great. last bit — cert/partner badge for Helio marketplace, we can coordinate joint marketing once tile is live. 00:09:31 Sofia Alvarez: marketing alignment needed but later. 00:09:34 Alex Morgan: ok let's do quick recap of owners and due dates. 00:09:38 Priya Desai: (recap) I'll produce an initial reference arch and sample log schema, Mina will produce terraform examples, Alex will send listing checklist and PR materials. Helio to provide test account. 00:09:52 Daniel Wu: thanks everyone. 00:09:54 Alex Morgan: thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links. 00:10:00 [meeting ends — recording continues for a few seconds]
notes: Transcript contains occasional ASR errors (e.g., 'KV cach' instead of KV cache, 'V-C-P' for VPC). Speakers used role labels; some cross talk removed. Links and artifacts will be shared via email and marketplace ticket.
